notes: Checks run from the repo root. A check that runs its work in a container or on another host (docker exec, kubectl exec, ssh) needs a 'cleanup' command: a check killed at the gate cap takes only its local client with it, so the gate runs 'cleanup' after a timeout, with the same $MYSPEC_CHECK_RUN_ID the check saw. Have the check record its remote PID in a file named after $MYSPEC_CHECK_RUN_ID, and have 'cleanup' kill that PID's process group. In a linked worktree, a check that runs a container exec (docker exec, docker container exec, docker compose exec, docker-compose exec, podman exec, podman-compose exec) without -w/--workdir is refused as unverifiable: it runs in the container's mount of the checkout the container or compose project was started from, usually the main checkout, so it would not verify the worktree. Mount the worktree in the container and pass -w with its path there, or run the tool on the host. The gate trusts -w without verifying it, so it must name the worktree's mount. Give a check a non-empty 'diffCommand' when its plain 'command' already fails on the default branch: the gate runs 'diffCommand' instead, with $MYSPEC_BASE_REF exported as the merge base with the default branch. Scope the command to that range and guard it against an empty file set, e.g. files=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR $MYSPEC_BASE_REF -- '*.ts'); [ -z "$files" ] || npx eslint $files
